name: Mexican Shredded Pork In Ancho-Orange Sauce (Chilorio)
headnote: Kate Williams writes up a recipe from Pati Jinich's cookbook Pati's Mexican Table as a dressed-up cousin of carnitas. Instead of plain slow-braised pork, the shoulder simmers in orange juice and water until the liquid cooks off and the meat browns in its own rendered fat, and it is then folded into a pureed ancho chile sauce sharpened with a lot of cider vinegar. Williams notes the combination reads almost like a Mexican take on pulled pork, and that the anchos and citrus work particularly well together. In her own testing she needed closer to an hour of simmering than the stated 40 to 45 minutes and topped the pot up with roughly another third of a cup of water and juice, and she stresses leaving the rendered fat and browned bits in the pot to flavor the sauce. Jinich also suggests swapping in bone-in, skin-on dark-meat chicken.
comment_digest: Substitutions get the most attention. One cook made it with chicken thighs and said his wife assumed it was pork; another used lard in place of the vegetable oil. Several report the dish reads sweet rather than hot, so do not scale the chiles back: one reviewer who reduced them wished she hadn't, and another left seeds in for heat and served it over creamy polenta. One cook swapped the stovetop reduction for the oven, boiling off the orange juice and browning the meat hands-off, slower but easier. Another used Kenji's chile prep, toasting the dried chiles and softening them in simmering chicken stock rather than plain hot water. Serving notes: shredded lettuce lightens a rich taco, and queso fresco with raw onion suits it. Two questions went unanswered: whether it freezes, and how to adapt the sauce to already-cooked leftover pork.
